title: EQUILIBRIUM (part 2)
textbookText: When the number of vehicles increases in the road, the chances of collision increases. In the same way the rate of reaction increases with increasing the concentration of the reacting substances. The relationship between the rate of reaction and concentration of reactants was given by Norwegian scientists Cato M. Guldberg and Peter Waagein the name of law of mass action.

Let us consider the following reaction, aA + bB → Products According to law of mass action, Rate of chemical reaction ∝ [A]a [B]b r = K[A]a [B]b Where, r= rate of reaction [A] = molar concentration of reactant A [B] = molar concentration of reactant B and K = proportionality constant called rate constant or velocity constant. a and b are the stoichiometric coefficients.

Law of mass action states, '' The rate at which a substance reacts is directly proportional to its molar concentration (active mass) and the rate of chemical reaction is directly proportional to the products of molar concentrations of reactants where each reactant term is raised to the power equal to stoichiometric coefficient seen in a balanced chemical equation''.

Do you know? In chemistry, Active mass and concentration are used to describe the amount of substance present, but they are different concepts. Active mass refers to the amount of a substance that is available to react in a chemical reaction. Concentration, on the other hand, refers to the amount of a substance present in a given volume of solution or mixture.
